# AxioDB

> The embedded database for Node.js. Replaces SQLite, LowDB, NeDB & raw JSON files with MongoDB-style queries, ACID transactions, and zero native dependencies. No node-gyp, no electron-rebuild, no `.node` binaries, no build step. Works on every platform Node.js ≥ 20 runs on. MIT licensed, actively maintained for Electron, CLI, local-first and prototyping. Current version: 21.7.8.

## What it is

AxioDB is a file-based embedded database for Node.js. It replaces SQLite, LowDB, NeDB, and raw JSON files with a single `npm install` — MongoDB-style queries, ACID transactions, InMemoryCache, and zero native C bindings. No compilation, no platform-specific builds, no ABI to match.

Sweet spot: 10K–500K documents per collection. Built for Electron apps, desktop software, CLI tools, local-first applications, and rapid prototyping.

## Why it exists: the SQLite/native-module problem

`better-sqlite3` and `node-sqlite3` ship compiled C binaries that must match your OS, CPU architecture, and Node/Electron ABI version. That produces node-gyp failures on machines without build tools, a mandatory `electron-rebuild` step re-run on every Electron upgrade, `NODE_MODULE_VERSION` mismatch crashes, per-platform CI builds, and Docker images that need a compiler just to install.

AxioDB is plain JavaScript reading and writing files. There is nothing to compile, nothing to rebuild, and nothing that can mismatch. That is the entire point.

## Why not LowDB, NeDB, or LokiJS?

**LowDB** stores everything in a single JSON file. No concurrency safety (concurrent writes corrupt data), no ACID transactions (crash = data loss), no built-in caching, entire DB loaded into memory. Last updated 3 years ago.

**NeDB** is abandoned since 2016. No security patches, no bug fixes. Users report data loss and file corruption. Callback-based API (no Promises). No TypeScript support.

**LokiJS** is in-memory only. No ACID transactions. Persistence is an afterthought. Abandoned.

**AxioDB** provides: file-per-document storage, ACID transactions with WAL, atomic writes via temp+rename, file-based locking, InMemoryCache, Worker Threads, TypeScript 6.0 strict, built-in GUI, TCP remote access, MCP server for AI agents. Actively maintained.

Full comparison: https://axiodb.in/comparison

## Key Differentiators

- Zero native dependencies (no node-gyp, no electron-rebuild, no `.node` files, no prebuilt-binary matrix)
- MongoDB-style queries: `{ age: { $gt: 25 } }` — not SQL strings. 19 query operators, plus index hints for query optimization.
- Built-in InMemoryCache (per-instance, configurable `minTTL`/`maxTTL`/`cacheClearUp`, `Cache: false` disables) with randomized TTL and selective invalidation
- Worker Threads for multi-core parallel processing
- ACID transactions with savepoints, rollback, and WAL — crash recovery covers plain `insert()` too, not just explicit transactions
- Atomic writes via temp file + rename — no data corruption on crash
- File-based locking with Wait-Die deadlock prevention — safe for concurrent access
- TCP transactions: BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK over TCP with savepoints, connection-pinned client proxy, and auto-rollback on disconnect
- Built-in web Dashboard on port 27018 with role-based login (Super Admin / Admin / View)
- AxioDBCloud: TCP remote access on port 27019, with optional shared-RBAC authentication (TCPAuth) and optional TLS
- CLI: Command line interface — TCP data operations and interactive REPL, HTTP database export/import, and HTTP user/role administration
- MCP Server: 43 tools for AI agent integration — **Docker image only, not in the npm package** (see below)
- Full TypeScript support (6.0 strict mode), types included, no `@types` package needed
- Index hints — force a specific index on any query with .hint('fieldName')
- Batch read — retrieve multiple documents by ID in one call with .findByIds([ids])

## Services and ports (important — these are not interchangeable)

| Service | Port | In npm package? | In Docker image? | Enable with |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Core embedded library | none | Yes | Yes | `new AxioDB()` |
| Dashboard (web GUI) | 27018 | Yes | Yes | `{ GUI: true }` / `AXIODB_GUI=true` |
| Dashboard HTTP API (REST, 41 endpoints) | 27018 | Yes | Yes | comes with the Dashboard; `{ HTTP: false }` disables it |
| AxioDBCloud TCP server | 27019 | Yes | Yes | `{ TCP: true }` / `AXIODB_TCP=true` |
| AxioDBCloud client | — | Yes | Yes | `require('axiodb').AxioDBCloud` |
| MCP server (43 tools) | 27020 | **No** | Yes | `AXIODB_MCP=true` |

The MCP server lives in the repository's `Docker/` directory, which is npm-ignored. `npm install axiodb` does not include it; the Docker image `theankansaha/axiodb` is the only supported way to run it.

None of these are hosted services. "AxioDBCloud" is the name of AxioDB's own TCP protocol and client, not a SaaS product — there is no account and no server operated on your behalf. Every port runs on your own machine or container. axiodb.in serves documentation only.

Port 27018 speaks HTTP. Port 27019 does **not** — it is a custom TCP protocol. Pointing an HTTP client at 27019 (or the AxioDBCloud client at 27018) is the most common setup error.

## Install

```bash
npm install axiodb
```

Requires Node.js >= 20.0.0. Server-side and desktop only — AxioDB needs a filesystem and does not run in a browser.

## Where it does not fit

Not for: 10M+ documents, multi-user web apps with hundreds of concurrent connections, relational data needing JOINs or foreign keys, replication/sharding/clustering, cross-collection transactions, or anything requiring SQL or an ORM (Prisma, Drizzle, Knex, TypeORM, Sequelize do not work with AxioDB). Updates are a flat shallow merge — `$inc`/`$set`/`$push` do not exist. Use PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or SQLite for those cases.

Machine-readable limits and the full boundary table: https://axiodb.in/llms-full.txt

## For AI Agents

- Every documentation page also returns Markdown when fetched with `Accept: text/markdown` (e.g. `curl -H "Accept: text/markdown" https://axiodb.in/usage`)
- [Agent Skill](https://axiodb.in/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json) — installable SKILL.md for working with AxioDB
- [OpenAPI 3.1](https://axiodb.in/openapi.json) — the AxioDB Dashboard HTTP API only (port 27018, runs wherever you run AxioDB — not hosted on axiodb.in, and not the TCP protocol on 27019 or the MCP server on 27020)
- [API catalog](https://axiodb.in/.well-known/api-catalog) — RFC 9727 linkset
- Content usage preferences are declared via `Content-Signal` in [robots.txt](https://axiodb.in/robots.txt): training, search, and AI input are all permitted
- In a WebMCP-capable browser this site registers three tools: `axiodb_list_docs`, `axiodb_read_doc`, `axiodb_search_docs`
